thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: node gpu-xg-17 reports repeated container restarts and kernel warnings: 'CUDA illegal memory access' — auto-escalating to #incidents :rotating_light:

Alex: ack, I'm on it. seeing C/R loops for runtime-server on gpu-xg-17. grabbing logs now.

Alex: kubectl logs -n runtime svc-runtime-2 -c runtime-server -f -> lots of 503s then crash, snippet:```\nE 03:14:12.345 runtime: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
stack: runtime::kernel_launch +0x1f2
stack: runtime::dispatch +0x3b
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  cudaMemcpy failed: an illegal memory access was encountered
```\n
Marta: if it's the new attention kernel we rolled last night that could explain an unaligned pointer hitting the kernel path. wheeled deploy 2.3.5? @deploy-bot what went out 02:50 UTC?

deploy-bot: Release 2.3.5 -> runtime-serve: tag=2.3.5, image=registry/redwood/runtime:2.3.5, rolled to prod at 02:48 UTC (canary 10% -> 100% at 02:55).

Samir: adding `dmesg | tail` from gpu-xg-17:```\n[ 12345.678901] runtime-server[3421]: segfault at 0x0 ip 00007f8a... sp 00007ffd... error 4 in libredwood_runtime.so[7f8a1c000000+1a0000]
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: RmHandler: RmH: GPU crash dump collected - reason: ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
[ 12345.679123] Out of memory: Kill process 3421 (runtime-server) score 123 or sacrifice child
```\n
Katie: quick customer note: noticing elevated 502/503s for a small subset of models (rt-large) starting 03:13 UTC. CS already opened a ticket with 7 customers reporting degradation. ETA for external comms?

Alex: for immediate mitigation I'm going to cordon+drain gpu-xg-17 and fail requests to fallback variant (quantized model on other nodes). taking node out of LB.

Marta: agree. also need to rollback runtime image to 2.3.4 on a small canary and monitor. there's a suspected race in KV cache eviction -> kernel path that some sequence lengths trigger.

Samir: running `kubectl drain gpu-xg-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. also pushing node-level nv driver logs to /tmp/crash-dumps.

Alex: drain started 03:20 UTC. new requests are being routed away. 03:22 saw immediate drop in 503s from 12% -> 4% globally.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook step 3: If GPU process crash with "illegal memory access", isolate node, collect full core dump, and rollback to last known-good runtime. See: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-crash#illegal-memory-access

Marta: prepping rollback playbook now. Samir, can you snapshot the pod logs and core dump before node reboot? we need those for kernel-team. run:```\nkubectl exec -n runtime -it svc-runtime-2 -- tar -czf /tmp/runtime-logs.tgz /var/log/runtime && cp /var/crash/core.* /tmp/ && gsutil cp /tmp/* gs://incidents/gpu-xg-17/1975002468/```\n
Samir: copying now. core dump ~1.8GB. ETA to upload 6m on 1Gbps.

Alex: Customer impact update for incident bridge: ~7 customers, ~12% of requests to model rt-large affected between 03:13–03:25 UTC. no data loss reported, requests retried by clients sometimes succeeded after fallback routing. status: degraded.

Katie: I'll draft customer-facing message: short note + mitigation steps + ETA for fix (rolling rollback). Will wait for final confirmation before send.

Marta: rolling back runtime to 2.3.4 on a canary group now (03:28). watching metrics.

deploy-bot: triggered rollback job -> runtime image set to registry/redwood/runtime:2.3.4 for deployment runtime-canary; progress: 10% -> 30% (03:31)

Alex: while rollback in progress, I'm keeping node drained and keeping a 10% throttling rule on heavy request sizes to protect remaining nodes. `rlimit` applied to routes /v1/generate for sequences >4096.

Oncall-L2: taking over primary pager from Alex at 03:45 UTC for next shift. Alex handing off: collected logs, core dump uploaded to gs://incidents/gpu-xg-17/1975002468/, node drained and reboot scheduled, rollback in progress on canary, customer comms drafted by Katie.

Alex: handing off. if rollback doesn't reduce crashes within 15m, we'll consider reverting the kernel module or disabling the new attention kernel path (Marta has the patch toggle).

Marta: can confirm canary nodes running 2.3.4 show no illegal access errors so far (03:36 -> 03:44). rolling to 100% planned if stable at 03:50.

Samir: node rebooted and rejoined at 03:54 UTC, health checks green. no further crash loops observed on gpu-xg-17 after rollback.

Katie: customer update sent at 03:55 UTC: "We've identified a runtime regression introduced in 2.3.5 causing GPU process crashes (illegal memory access) for a subset of requests. We've rolled back the runtime and routed traffic to fallback variants; affected customers should see normalized behavior. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with postmortem." :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> status changed to MONITORING. severity downgraded from P1 to P2 at 03:57 UTC.

Marta: next steps: kernel-team to analyze core dump & nv driver crash dump, reproduce locally with model traces (sequence length distribution attached), add guarded checks in attention kernel for unaligned pointers, investigate race in KV cache eviction ordering. I'll open an internal bug linking the core dump and stack traces.

Oncall-L2: taking notes for postmortem: timeline, deploy 2.3.5, crash signatures (illegal memory access + OOM), rollback 2.3.4, customer impact ~42m window, no data exfiltration, next action: schedule kernel-team deep-dive and add test that fuzzes alignment on attention kernels.

Alex: thanks everyone. leaving this thread for postmortem write-up. marking handoff complete.
